adjacent_skills: real-time embedded software for distributed electro-mechanical systems (internship-scope only, no full-time)
hardware bring-up / SIL / HIL infra (has bring-up, not named SIL/HIL)
sensor/actuator integration (robotics domain, not automotive ECU)
key_responsibilities: Build/contribute to simulation, emulation, SIL, and HIL infrastructure for drive control validation
Design/develop/test embedded software for autonomous trajectory execution into actuator commands (motor torque, brake torque, steering angle)
Contribute to control source arbitration and safety monitoring across trajectory execution and drive control ECUs
Integrate supplier sub-systems (steering, motoring, braking, active suspension) into the Zoox software stack
Cross-functional work with Motion & Controls, Vehicle Dynamics, Safety Systems, Validation teams

strengths: Object Tracking Turret: YOLOv8-on-Jetson detection driving STM32 over UART, multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven commands and user override, FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination — the user-override path is a real, if small-scale, analog to the arbitration-between-control-sources concept in the JD

STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor: peripheral-level bare-metal C, timer-triggered ADC, interrupt-driven sampling, deterministic 1Hz loop, verified in Proteus — shows real embedded rigor and simulation-before-hardware discipline

COFFIN robotic arm: resolved 11 integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, false positives) across a Jetson+Arduino distributed pipeline, plus dual ToF sensor gating before the gripper closes — genuine hands-on bring-up/debug experience and a safety-gate-before-actuation pattern

Autonomous Driving in CARLA: adaptive control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback validated across multiple laps with traffic — the closest thing in the profile to an actual AV software stack, even though it is simulation-only
real_gaps: No exposure to vehicle networks at all — CAN and LIN are not just missing keywords, the whole mental model of a distributed automotive ECU network is unbuilt; all his multi-device comms is UART/I2C/SPI on hobbyist boards

No actual torque/force-based actuator control — his actuator experience is servo PWM position control (turret, robotic arm), not the motor torque / brake torque / steering angle control loops the JD is built around
No SIL/HIL in the industrial sense the JD means — Proteus and CARLA are real but hobbyist/research-scale simulation, not hardware-in-the-loop rigs validating against real supplier hardware

No safety-critical process experience — ISO-26262 lifecycle, MISRA static analysis, requirements traceability (Polarion) are all absent; every project is personal/capstone scope with no certification process behind it

No supplier-subsystem integration experience — the JD explicitly wants integrating third-party steering/motor/brake/suspension modules as black boxes with their own protocols; his hardware integration is always self-owned/self-designed
Zero full-time industry experience, and none of the 7 internships touch automotive
overstated_by_keywords: FreeRTOS counted as satisfying the RTOS requirement, but it is hobbyist-scale (turret project) — a different tier from the certified/safety-rated RTOS usage (QNX, SafeRTOS) a safety-critical automotive JD implies
sensor/actuator integration counted as a Have, but it is servo/PWM/GPIO-level integration of self-owned hardware, not the supplier black-box integration the JD describes
hardware bring-up credited as a partial preferred-have, but it is breadboard/single-board scale, not full-vehicle ECU bring-up
llm_analysis.reasoning: The embedded fundamentals (C/C++, FreeRTOS, real-time interrupt-driven design, hardware bring-up) are genuinely there and transferable, which is what keeps this from being a clean reject. But the role is built around automotive vehicle networks, torque-based actuator control, and a safety-certified development process, and none of that exists anywhere in the profile even adjacently, so the real distance is bigger than the 70% keyword match suggests.

outcome.notes: Hiring manager passed after Sep 9 recruiter screen with Mikel Pounds (Zoox technical recruiter, firmware roles). Recruiter redirected to the Body Systems team req instead.
